Visit note | 2025-05-06 11:00 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Tasnim Miah, 60, female. Mrs. Miah reports feeling a tight chest when exposed to dust or cold air along with coughing at night. She works as a shopkeeper, and her symptoms flared during the winter smog in Tongi. She has no known comorbidities and denies fever or chest pain at rest. Examination reveals: SpO2 93%, BP 133/80 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 51 kg. Auscultation reveals widespread wheezing with clear breath sounds otherwise. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up in 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-05-06 02:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Jewel Pramanik, 31, male. Mr. Pramanik complains of frequent sneezing fits and symptoms that worsen with dust. He works as a garment factory worker, and his discomfort has been worse since road construction began near his home in Khilgaon. He has no chronic illnesses and reports no sinus pain or fever. Visit note | 2025-05-06 02:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Arifa Matubbar, 67, female. Mrs. Matubbar describes having her eyelids stuck together in the morning and a red eye. On examination: visual acuity 6/12 in the left eye, BP 123/76 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 73 kg. Visit note | 2025-05-06 02:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Zahid Bhuiyan, 43, male. Mr. Bhuiyan attends for review regarding a stiff shoulder for weeks, being unable to reach behind the back, and night pain in the shoulder. He works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver, and his condition started after weeks of keeping the arm still after a sprain in Barishal. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Examination shows: shoulder lifts only to 105 degrees, BP 131/81 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 90 kg. Joint movement is restricted in all planes with tenderness around the capsule. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Examination reveals: platelet count 61000 per microlitre, temperature 102.6°F, BP 120/86 mmHg, pulse 103 bpm, weight 87 kg. Abdomen is soft without organomegaly. Assessment: Dengue fever. She was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.
